# Competitive Workflow Editor UX

Reference file for Dimension 6. All citations reference [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Platform Comparison

| Platform | Canvas Library | State Management | Layout | Language |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|--------|----------|
| **n8n** | Vue Flow (Vue 3) [11] | Pinia stores [11] | Grid-snapped (20px) [11] | TypeScript [11] |
| **Node-RED** | Custom (D3 + jQuery) [12] | Server-side (Express) [12] | Flow-based [12] | JavaScript [12] |
| **Retool Workflows** | Proprietary [14] | Internal [14] | Autolayout [14] | Blocks [14] |

## n8n Architecture

n8n's canvas is built on Vue Flow with a layered component hierarchy [11]:
`NodeView.vue` → `WorkflowCanvas` → `Canvas.vue` (Vue Flow wrapper) → `CanvasNode.vue`

The `useCanvasMapping` composable bridges n8n's internal `INodeUi` objects and Vue Flow's
graph model [11]. Operations go through `useCanvasOperations` with history command support
(AddNodeCommand, MoveNodeCommand, etc.) for undo/redo [11].

Collaborative editing uses WebSocket synchronization with presence pills and user
activity detection [11].

## Node-RED Architecture

Built on Express.js with WebSocket real-time communication between editor and runtime [12].
The runtime uses a node registry pattern (`registry.js`) for discovering and loading
installed node types [12]. The architecture separates editor (browser) from runtime
(server), connected via REST API and WebSocket [12].

Note: Architecture overview is described as outdated (3+ years old) [12].

## Retool Workflows

Canvas-based IDE with unconstrained drag-and-drop [14]. Features:
- Minimap with draggable highlight indicator [14]
- Graph view (standard) and Tree view (vertical) toggle [14]
- Autolayout for algorithmic block positioning [14]
- Outline panel for hierarchical block listing with filtering [14]
- Function blocks as reusable components (separate tab) [14]
- Multi-environment support (production, staging) [14]

## Windmill

DAG execution model with OpenFlow JSON standard [13]. Uniquely supports both visual
builder and workflows-as-code (TypeScript, Python, Go, PHP, Bash, SQL) [13]. "Each step
is code" producing results passed to dependent steps [13].

Visual builder features: branching, for/while loops, approval steps with suspensions,
error handlers, caching, concurrency limits, priority queuing, AI-generated flows [13].

## Cloudflare Workflows

Code-first approach with automatic diagram generation from TypeScript ASTs [18]. Uses
oxc-parser via WebAssembly to analyze bundled JavaScript at deployment time [18].
Tracks Promise/await relationships for execution ordering [18]. 14 predefined node
types covering steps, loops, branching, parallelism [18].

## UX Design Principles

Customer.io's workflow builder evolution identified 5 principles [23]:

1. **Approachable**: Simple automations should feel simple
2. **Empowering**: Enable capability growth through visual feedback
3. **Holistic**: Display entire workflow with sidebar editing for context
4. **Unambiguous**: All actions immediately apparent
5. **Intuitive**: "Matches the customer's mental model" [23]

The key insight: users sketch campaigns as flow diagrams on whiteboards. Aligning the
builder to this mental model reduced cognitive load [23].

| Autolayout | Retool [14], Windmill [13] |
| Sidebar editing | Customer.io [23], Retool [14] |
| View mode toggle | Retool (graph/tree) [14] |
| Trigger-based execution | Retool (webhook/schedule) [14], n8n [11] |
| Collaborative editing | n8n (WebSocket) [11] |

## Editor Scalability

- n8n/Node-RED: cited as becoming unwieldy beyond ~100 nodes on visual canvas [41]
- Customer.io: rewrote layout algorithm to support "ten times larger" workflows [23]
- Retool: unconstrained canvas implies no hard limit [14]
